title: Answer: gravity is the surface tension of the vacuum crystal, with no graviton

statements.text: Gravity is not a fundamental force carried by a spin-2 graviton. It is an emergent surface tension of the discrete vacuum: boundary defect areas grow sub-additively, $A \propto M^{2/3}$, so the vacuum merges defects to minimize stress, which yields the inverse-square law.

sources.quote: Gravitational attraction is the strict mathematical consequence of the sub-additive geometry of topological boundary tension.
Gravity is simply the emergent surface tension of a discrete vacuum crystal
